written_before: any RELIEF variant was built or any REPORT-ONLY proxy (hide-and-recover, SGMC control, block CV) was computed for a RELIEF arm
why_this_axis: MASS, PRUNE, CONCENTRATION and SNAP are already in ledger/submissions.csv (17 rows); RELIEF is the first unbuilt axis in the brief's default order (SPACING is lowest priority, TRACKB is Phase 2). The human left AXIS unassigned and asked the agent to pick.

design.relief_field: training_features.tif Band 12 det_elev (detrended elevation), -3.4e38 sentinels inside the footprint replaced by the footprint median; terciles by footprint AREA so each class holds one third of the 5,167,373 footprint pixels
design.dose: 12% of N = 37,654 -> 4,518 dots moved (inside the brief's 10-15% band; one dose, three directions)
direction_variants: basin12: donors = piedmont + range -> receiver = basin
pied12: donors = basin + range -> receiver = piedmont
range12: donors = basin + piedmont -> receiver = range
design.donor_rule: each donor tercile loses the same FRACTION of its movable dots (proportional thinning), so a 'toward X' variant does not silently become a single-tercile swap
design.frozen: R0's 2,171 collar dots (2 < d_cat <= 3 px) are never donors; all added dots sit at d_cat > 3 px on un-emitted H19-5 ridge pixels; count fixed at 37,654
design.within_tercile_ranking: exact iterative marginal expected-DTI gain under the same label-free physics field used for PRUNEp3px (scripts/build_prune_variants.py, 15 canary-checked channels), identical machinery for drops and adds in all three arms so that differences BETWEEN arms isolate relief

basin12.reason: basin interiors are blanketed by Quaternary fill; faults there are blind and rarely enter expert-mapped label sets, so dots moved onto basin H19-5 ridges mostly pay S without T

pied12.reason: piedmont already holds R0's highest dot density (9.1 per 1,000 px); new Quaternary scarp mapping (lidar) concentrates here, but marginal H19-5 ridge pixels in this tercile are the most depleted

range12.reason: bedrock exposure in ranges lets geologists map faults directly; compilations beyond the USGS/INGENIOUS Quaternary catalogue (e.g. state geologic maps) are dominated by bedrock range faults, and R0 under-weights the range tercile (37.7% of dots vs 63.6% of off-catalogue SGMC fault pixels, which was visible in the exploration run before this file was written)

disclosure: The off-catalogue SGMC tercile shares (basin 11.3%, piedmont 25.1%, range 63.6%) were printed by the exploration script BEFORE these predictions were written, so the range12 prior is not blind to the SGMC control. The per-arm SGMC DTI values were not computed before this file was written.
falsification_rule: treat any live change under 0.01 in absolute value as no evidence (public chunks only); a direction is confirmed only if its receipt exceeds R0 by >= 0.01 AND the opposite direction does not
